Amar Singh R/o Village Khamariya, PO-Nanakmatta, Sitarganj, U.S. Nagar, Uttrakhand. ............Driver-cum-owner/Respondent no.1 2. Nationanl Insurance Company Ltd. 301-303, Sahyog Building Nehru Place, New Delhi-110019. ............Insurance company/Respondent no.2 Date of accident : 10.09.2018 Result of accident : Injury(Permanent disability) Date of filing of Petition : 25.01.2021 Date of Decision : 02.04.2025 Mact No.71/21 Kanhaiya Singh v. Jaswant Singh P.No. 1 Of 21 Bk Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Sh. Kanhaiya Singh suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 10.09.2018 at about 11.30 pm, when petitioner/injured was standing on the roadside near village-Mundeli, then motorcycle bearing no.UK-06- AR-4914 came from the side of Khatima in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner resulting in grievous injuries to injured on his head and all over the body. Petitioner initially went to Prayas Hospital, Khatima and thereafter was referred to higher center. Kanhaiya Singh vs Jaswant Singh on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45960272/ 1 3. An FIR no.377/18 was registered u/s 279,338 of IPC PS Khatima, Distt-U.S.Nagar. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 5. No Written statement or reply filed on behalf of Respondent no.1 despite opportunity. Respondent no.2/insurance company filed reply submitting that driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, however, it admitted that offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident. 6. Vide order dated 14.01.2022, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a MACT NO.71/21 Kanhaiya Singh v. Jaswant Singh P.No. 2 Of 21 BK road traffic accident on 10.09.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UK-06AR-4914 being driven & owned by R1 and insured with R2? OPP 2. Whether the injured is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner Kanhaiya Singh led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1 by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the claim petition. He further deposed that he was working as Manager with Style & Fashion Garment store and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. He spent Rs.2,50,000/- on attendant, Rs.2,50,000/- on special diet, Rs.25,00,000/- on treatment and future treatment would be of Rs.10,00,000/-, Rs.2,50,000/- on conveyance. He suffered 75% permanent disability in relation to right and upper lower limbs alongwith intellectual impairment. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1, educational documents as Ex.PW-1/2, original medical prescriptions as Ex.PW-1/3, original medical bills as Ex.PW-1/4, FIR as Ex.PW-1/5, site plan as Ex.PW-1/6, chargesheet as Ex.PW-1/7, driving licnece of respondent-1/driver-cum-owner Jaswant Singh as Ex.PW-1/8, RC of offending vehicle as Ex.PW-1/9, insurance policy of offending vehicle s Ex.PW-1/10. He was cross- examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/Respondent no.2. Sh. Jitendra Singh was examined as PW-2. He tender his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW-2/A. He deposed that he is the Proprietor of Style & Fashion Garment Store, Tehsil Road, MACT NO.71/21 Kanhaiya Singh v. Jaswant Singh P.No. 3 Of 21 BK Subzi Mandi chowk, Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand. He is running the business of sale & purchase of ready-made garments including stitching of school uniforms. He deposed that petitioner/injured Kanhaiya Singh was working in his store as a Manager and was permanent employee. He was drawing salary of Rs.20,000/- p.m. After his accident on 10.09.2018, he was unable to continue working as Manager Kanhaiya Singh vs Jaswant Singh on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45960272/ 2 in his company due to his injuries/permanent disability. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-2/1, PAN card as Ex.PW-2/2, GST Registration document of his company as Ex.PW-2/3, Income tax return as Ex.PW-2/4, bank account statement as Ex.PW-2/5. He was not cross-examined by any of the respondents. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, MACT NO.71/21 Kanhaiya Singh v. Jaswant Singh P.No. 4 Of 21 BK in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. In the instant case, petitioner/injured Kanhaiya Singh has examined himself to prove the factum as well as manner of accident. He has categorically stated that the accident occurred with the offending motorcycle at the time when he was walking by the side of the road. He has specifically alleged that the offending motorcycle was being driven at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. MACT NO.71/21 Kanhaiya Singh v. Jaswant Singh P.No. 5 Of 21 BK Kanhaiya Singh vs Jaswant Singh on 2 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45960272/ 3 12. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
